details:
The Idea:

VRChat just announced they are moving to a new support for URP. For years, there were a lot of cool features that world creators wanted, but they were impossible to add because the old graphics pipeline couldn't handle them.

Now that we are upgrading to URP, can we finally add these long-requested features?

Features We Would Love to See:

- FPS Boosters (DLSS & FSR): VR takes a higher performance computer to run smoothly. URP makes it easier to add "upscalers." This is a smart technology that helps the game run way faster without making it look ugly. It would be a lifesaver for PC players with lag.

-- Native implementation of modern temporal upscaling like DLSS and AMD FSR 2.0+ was incredibly difficult under Unity's Built-In Render Pipeline (BiRP). URP provides a much cleaner pipeline for injecting these upscalers, which is critical for PCVR overhead.

- Smart Eye-Tracking: A lot of new VR headsets can track exactly where your eyes are looking. With URP, the game could learn to only draw exactly what you are staring at in super-high detail. The blurry stuff in the corner of your eye doesn't need to be perfect. This saves a ton of computer power!

-- Dynamic Foveated Rendering (DFR) relies on targeted resolution scaling based on eye-tracking data. BiRP and EAC made this a nightmare to implement natively, but URP’s architecture natively supports much better integration for foveated rendering passes.

- Stickers and Splatters (Decals): We want an easy way to put "stickers" on the world. Things like bullet holes in shooting games, footprints on the floor, or paint splatters. Right now, doing this makes the game super laggy, but URP has a fast, built-in way to handle it.

- In BiRP, dynamic details require clunky particle system hacks or the old Projector component, which breaks batching and tanks performance. URP features a highly optimized Decal Projector system that allows for performant, batched screen-space decals.

- Real Reflections and Shadows: Right now, making shiny puddles, real mirrors, or good shadows slows down the game a lot. URP gives world makers an easy way to add realistic lighting and reflections without ruining everyone's framerate.

-- Creators currently rely on heavy custom shaders, Post-Processing V2 hacks, or completely baked lighting for occlusion and reflections. URP includes built-in, globally optimized render passes for Screen Space Ambient Occlusion (SSAO) and Screen Space Reflections (SSR).

- Better Portals and Sniper Scopes: Right now, looking through a sniper scope or a portal basically cuts your game speed in half because the game has to draw the world twice. URP is much better at handling extra cameras, making these items run smoothly.

-- Secondary cameras and Render Textures in BiRP carry massive performance overhead. URP utilizes camera stacking and handles render targets much more efficiently, drastically reducing the draw call penalty for in-game scopes, mirrors, and portals.

Why this matters:

People have been asking for these things for years, and the answer was usually "we can't do that yet." Since the game engine is finally getting this massive update, it's the perfect time to start adding them!
title: Use the New "URP" Update to add "on-hold" features
